activeContracts.contract: Apps uses the shared Home inventory with own shortcuts excluded from installed items. Its menu derives isFavorite from six known first IDs and writes remaining+selected on removal through the existing snapshot save boundary.

Home and embedded Apps share icon inventory. Home nonempty saved order applies known inventory and takes six. Home injects Music, Calls, Tools, Settings and Store only if their icons prepare; dashboard also requires configuration.
Save still compares the retained order and reloads canonical state; builtin component identities match the actual Home injected entries, including fixed Calls sentinel.

saveOrderFromSnapshot remains under the companion mutation lock and refuses stale logical order. Existing codec de-duplicates; applyOrder discards unknown IDs only from display and appends the remaining actual inventory.

witness.generatedInput: Six distinct installed app IDs A..F, saved order empty, actual available Store shortcut, selected A already in Apps first six.
witness.before: Old saved order B,C,D,E,F,A keeps A in the six Home/Apps favorites despite Remove.
witness.after: New order B,C,D,E,F,Store,other known builtins,A puts at least six actual available non-selected IDs before A; both projections exclude A.
witness.minimumHomeGuarantee: At least six distinct IDs other than the selected app are genuinely available in the Home inventory and represented ahead of the selected app after this save.

priorScopeDistinction: The positive UserLayout conflict receipt preserves old favorite-order semantics and verifies stale-save protection. This review addresses the installed-only removal candidate list while keeping that snapshot boundary and all persistence rules unchanged.
limits: Independent host source review and parsing retained baseline XML only. Reviewer performed no tests, build, SDK, Git, device, registry, media, provider, network or account operation.
Current full build, candidate JVM outcome, native fixture, APK/signature/assets and room promotion remain separate root-owned gates; none is claimed passed here.

Frozen JVM fixture invokes the actual private compiled menu callback and actual UserLayout persistence through mocked generated Context/preferences and AppItems. Home/Apps first-six projections are source-derived; no mounted Compose menu, physical interaction or real PackageManager/icon inventory acceptance.

The one-installed-app/six-shortcut generated case assumes all six Home shortcuts exist, including configured dashboard. With only five actual Home shortcuts and one app, Remove cannot exclude that app from the existing six-slot policy; scarce or missing-icon alternatives are not solved.

Apps already admits an unconfigured dashboard as a known builtin key. That virtual membership, actual dashboard/icon availability and any Home/Apps inventory mismatch are unchanged and excluded from the guarantee.

Existing `(ordered IDs + order)` prefix already places installed IDs before saved shortcut records. The change preserves that prior semantic; it does not promise to preserve original shortcut positions or redesign favorites.
Stale unknown IDs remain persisted in their existing relative prefix position; duplicates remain normalized by existing distinct/codec rules. No new persistence/settings/UI design.
No broad concurrent-edit/raw-writer/disk-durability, optimized/API28 or live household acceptance claim.
